MINUTES

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  APRIL 10, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at
7:02 p.m. in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman.

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Administrative Services Director Michael Whitehead
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION – DMV/DONATE LIFE CALIFORNIA MONTH - APRIL

  MAYOR HUFF presented a proclamation recognizing April as DMV/Donate Life
  California Month. One Legacy Ambassador and heart transplant recipient, George
  Happe was present to accept the proclamation on behalf of the organization and share
  his story.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE ITEMS A-E AS PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 10, 2018
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the City
  Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF MARCH 27, 2018

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – APRIL 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 59773 THROUGH 59799 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $73,635.73 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 26, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  AUTHORITY TO DESTROY OBSOLETE RECORDS

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

  Tom Judge, 28 Rollingwood Drive expressed concern regarding the roadway striping and
  traffic markings/delineation at the intersection of Silver Spur Road and Kingspine Road
  as a result of the street resurfacing.

  In response to Mr. Judge’s concern, Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer stated that
  when the resurfacing is complete, all of the traffic markings, including the candlesticks,
  will be replaced exactly as they were before the street resurfacing.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS (7:30 P.M.)

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 29-16: PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Open the Public Hearing; 2) Take public
  testimony; 3) Discuss the issues; and 4) Close the Public Hearing; 5) Adopt Resolution
  No. 2416 adopting a Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and
  Reporting Program for the project; and 6) Adopt Resolution No. 2417, approving
  Variances, a Conditional Use Permit and Grading Permit for project-related grading.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and reviewed
  the additional materials received since the agenda packet was distributed including a
  clarifying technical memo from the City’s consultant, ESA, regarding the operational
  noise from the pump station and several items of correspondence from neighboring
  properties.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 10, 2018
   She further provided information as to how the issues raised at the last meeting have
  been addressed and reviewed the modified conditions included in the revised resolution
  to specifically address those issues.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding the geotechnical issues raised at
  the last meeting, Planning Director Wahba stated that once the building plans are
  submitted for approval, the Building Official well ensure that the geotechnical
  requirements are being met.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, regarding the equestrian issues raised
  at the Equestrian Committee meeting, MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL noted that those
  issues are still pending and staff will continue to monitor.

  Carmelo Sorce, Director of Engineering, California Water Service Company and Chad
  Brown, Design Builder, Black & Veatch reviewed a PowerPoint presentation providing
  detailed responses to the issues raised at the last meeting regarding the aesthetics of
  the pump station building, the vibration from the pump station, the noise from the
  pump station and the seismic design of the pipeline itself. Mr. Sorce further commented
  that in response to inquiry regarding the possibility of installing additional fire hydrants,
  there is sufficient pressure to install three additional hydrants on Crenshaw Boulevard
  between Palos Verdes Drive North and the pump station.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF regarding the seismic integrity of the pipeline
  material, Mr. Sorce stated that have explored various pipeline material and they believe
  the material they have selected the right material for this project.

  Regarding the aesthetics of the pump house, COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN
  commented that he prefers the ranch style architecture.

  MAYOR HUFF called for public comment.

  Tim Buresh, Civil Engineer, 5 Single Tree Lane spoke in support of the project and
  encouraged the City Council to approve the project. He expressed general concern
  regarding the traffic impacts of the project should construction on Palos Verdes Drive
  North be delayed into the school year.

  Carol Reinhart, 4339 Canyon View Lane (RPV) thanked Cal Water and staff for listening
  to their concerns and encouraged the City Council to include the revised conditions as
  presented, to require that the lighting plan include a provision that the lights only be on
  when the site is accessed; and to approve a Mediterranean style for the pump house.

  Doug Deecy, 27938 Beechgate Drive (RPV) expressed continued concern regarding
  vibration from the pump equipment.

  Edie Beachboard, Canyon View Lane spoke in general support of the project; but
  expressed concern that their neighborhood did not find out about the project until
  recently.

  Corrie Watts, 27243 Eastvale Road (PVP) spoke in support of the installation of
  additional fire hydrants on Crenshaw Boulevard.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 10, 2018
   COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that detailed information regarding the
  project timeline, expected traffic impact and road closures is also available through
  several website including the project web site.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided an overview of the entire route for the new pipeline.

  Chad Brown, Design Builder, Black & Veatch reviewed a detailed timeline for the project
  including construction hours, traffic impacts, road closures, traffic control measures
  and equestrian trail impacts.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding penalties for delay in the
  project completion, Mr. Sorce commented that there are contractual liquidated damages
  built into the contract for overall completion of the project.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR HUFF SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented with regard to the architectural style for the
  pump house, the Mediterranean style blends well into surrounding area and since it is
  what the neighbors prefer, she is supportive of it. She further commented that she is
  also support of the installation of additional fire hydrants along Crenshaw Blvd; and
  that the other issues raised regarding vibration and noise have been sufficiently
  addressed and she is supportive of the project with the changes to the resolution as
  proposed.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPTED RESOLUTION NO. 2416, ADOPTING A
  MITIGATED NEGATIVE DECLARATION AND MONITORING AND REPORTING
  PROGRAM FOR THE PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2416 by title only.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2417 APPROVING
  VARIANCES, A CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT AND GRADING PERMIT FOR
  PROJECT-RELATED GRADING AS AMENDED TO INCLUDE THE REVISED
  CONDITIONS AND REQUIRING A MEDITERRANEAN ARCHITECTURAL STYLE
  FOR PUMP HOUSE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution No. 2417 by title only.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 10, 2018
 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  BID RESULTS – STORM DRAIN REHABILITATION PROJECT (Taken out of order)

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid to Southwest Pipeline and
  Trenchless Corp. in the amount of $394,825 for the 2017-18 Storm Drain Rehabilitation
  Project and allocate a 10% contingency in the amount of $39,482.50 to address any
  unforeseen issues related to the storm drain repairs.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN questioned if the amount of contingency is high
  enough given that the majority of the work associated with this project is underground.
  In response, Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that staff believes the 10%
  contingency is enough; but there are sufficient funds in the budget allocated to this
  project so that if the City Council wished to increase the contingency, it could do so.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AWARD THE BID TO SOUTHWEST PIPELINE AND
  TRENCHLESS CORP. IN THE AMOUNT OF $394,825 FOR THE 2017-18 STORM
  DRAIN REHABILITATION PROJECT AND ALLOCATE A 10% CONTINGENCY IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $39,482.50 TO ADDRESS ANY UNFORESEEN ISSUES
  RELATED TO THE STORM DRAIN REPAIRS

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  AMENDMENT TO CONTRACT WITH MARJANI BUILDERS – ADDITION OF ADDITIVE
  ALTERNATIVE BID D, CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER RENOVATION (Taken out of order)

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve a contract amendment with Marjani
  Builders to include Additive Alternative Bid D, City Council Chamber, in the amount of
  $166,000 all to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per agenda
  material). He noted that the total bid award including Base Bid B and Additive
  Alternative Bid D is $319,000 plus a 15% contingency.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, Administrative Services Director noted that since the City
  Council Chambers also serve as a Community Center, used for various community
  meetings and events, the City will utilize its QUIMBY funds and PEG fees to at least
  partially fund this portion of the project.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUKERMAN regarding the method by which this bid
  was obtained, Administrative Services Director Whitehead commented that this portion
  of the project was included in the original bid documents for the entire City Hall/Council
  Chamber Renovation project as an additive/alternative item at the City’s discretion
  whether or not to award.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
APRIL 10, 2018
   In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead reviewed the proposed upgrades to the Council Chamber facility.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that his is not in favor of simple aesthetic
  improvements, but to the degree there is a public benefit to the project, he would be
  supportive of the project. He suggested that a better use of QUIMBY funds might be for
  an efficient irrigation system at all of the City’s parks.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that in its current state, the Council
  Chambers do not function well as a community room and she believes that the
  community would benefit greatly by making the room more functional for community
  use in general.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE AMENDING THE CONTRACT WITH
  MARJANI BUILDERS TO INCLUDE ADDITIVE ALTERNATIVE BID D, CITY
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, IN THE AMOUNT OF $166,000 TO THE SATISFACTION OF
  THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  NONE.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports
  to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently active
  Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations, special
  districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various committees on which Members of the City
  Council might serve or have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM: 702 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE – SHORT
  TIME LIMIT PARKING REQUEST (COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ)

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) remove, repair or replace traffic signs on
  Palos Verdes Drive East as noted on Exhibits A-1 and A-2 of the staff report; and 2)
  remove the guardrail on the south side of Palos Verdes Drive East and repair the
  guardrail on the north side.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN with regard to the survey that was sent
  to businesses in the area, Assistant City Manager Grammer commented that the results
  were not overwhelmingly in support of a short time parking limit.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
APRIL 10, 2018
   In response COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, regarding the removal of the red curb,
  Traffic Engineer Itagaki commented that she sees no need for 40 ft. of red curb and is
  supportive of removing 20 ft. of the red curb.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ expressed appreciation to Assistant City Manager
  Grammer for finding a creative solution to this issue.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO: 1) PREPARE A RESOLUTION FOR
  CITY COUNCIL APPROVAL IMPLEMENTING A 24-MINUTE PARKING
  RESTRICTION AND 20’ GREEN CURB IN FRONT OF 702 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE;
  AND 2) REMOVE 20’ OF RED CURB AT 655 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

B.  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CUB / CHANDLER RANCH
  ROAD (COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ)

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material). Traffic
  Engineer Itagaki provided her assessment of the intersection and the reasons why no
  changes to the existing conditions were recommended.

  Discussion ensued concerning the conditions at the intersection and options for
  improving visibility at the intersection including removing a portion 3-rail fencing,
  adding some other sort of barrier and realigning stop bar. Further discussion ensued
  concerning traffic speeds and traffic calming strategies for Palos Verdes Drive East.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that in a discussion with a Councilmember
  from the City of Lomita concerning the roadway condition on Narbonne Avenue between
  Pacific Coast Highway and the City limit, it was suggested that part of the declining
  roadway condition could have been caused by the traffic from construction vehicles
  going to and from the Country Club. Discussion ensued concerning the roadway
  condition on Narbonne Avenue between Pacific Coast Highway and the City limit. City
  Manager Prichard commented that staff will look into ways to improve the roadway
  condition.

  Following discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to:

  DIRECT STAFF TO FURTHER ASSES THE VISIBILITY CONDITIONS FROM
  CHANDLER RANCH ROAD AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST AND PROVIDE A
  RECOMMENDATION FOR IMPROVING THE VISIBILITY CONDITIONS AT THE
  NEXT MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL.

** OTHER REPORTS **

MAYOR HUFF reminded those present and watching about several upcoming events including
the City’s Earth Day Celebration including free paper shredding on Wednesday, April 18 from
3:00 p.m. – 6:00 p.m. at Promenade on the Peninsula; Community Meeting on Coyote: Wildlife
Watch on April 18 at 6:30 p.m. at Hesse Park in RPV and subsequent Wildlife Watch Trainings
on April 18,

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
APRIL 10, 2018
 COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN reminded those present and watching that the Mayor’s
Breakfast Ride and Boy Scouts Pancake Breakfast will be held on May 5.

COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN provided an update on the status of Clean Power Alliance of
Southern California.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on currently
  pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

  NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

  NONE.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:41 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to the next regular
  meeting of the City Council to be held on Tuesday, April 24, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the
  Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California. (Closed Session beginning at 5:30 p.m.)

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
APRIL 10, 2018
